rendered:
The document does not support the premise: the authors did not pick the value in your question as optimal. They chose 165 μM[1] of 4-MPBA[2] as the optimized condition. The value 120 μM[3] appears only as the top of the concentration range in the redispersion-stability test.

Reasons given for the choice:
1. CD response: the CD intensity reached its maximum at 165 μM[4], followed by a decrease at higher concentrations[5]. Raising the concentration to 225 μM[6] resulted in only marginal changes in the CD signal[7].
2. Redispersion stability: the 165 μM 4-MPBA-derived[8] BA@L-HGNRs showed exceptional spectral stability[9] over the whole monitoring period in NH4HCO3 buffer, which the authors took as confirmation that the modification improved colloidal redispersion stability.
3. Decision: that concentration was set as the optimized condition for all subsequent experiments.

Note that the text is internally inconsistent about the range. It says the concentration was tuned from 0 to 120 μM[10], yet it later describes increases up to 225 μM[11]. The document gives no explicit reason for the range stopping at the lower value.
